comparisons.questionText: Do you see a niche within your target market that you can serve?

pre.answer: Young people who likes to learn new cultures (something similar to Duolingo? lol)

post.answer: This is what ChatGPT told me and those niches are what exactly I have been working on: Given your unique positioning as a multilingual Thai student living in China, sharing cultural, travel, and lifestyle content with humor, you have several niche opportunities. The key is to find the intersection of interests where demand is high, but competition is relatively low. Potential Niches You Can Own: 1. Thai in China - The Ultimate Guide for Thai Students & Expats in China: Intersection: Thai students & expats + Life in China + Humor + Practical Tips. Why this niche works: Many Thai students and professionals are interested in studying or working in China but don't have enough first-hand, relatable content to guide them. Most content on studying abroad in China is generic or from non-Thai perspectives—you can create a Thai-centered approach. You already have the authenticity & experience—you're living it! Content Ideas: Thai Student's Survival Guide to China - Visa, scholarships, dorm life, culture shock, must-have apps, networking, etc. Thai Food vs. Chinese Food Series - Fun food comparisons & trying Chinese food as a Thai person. How to Make Friends in China as a Thai Student - Thai-Chinese social & cultural differences. Funny Thai-Chinese Language Mix-ups - Hilarious misunderstandings in daily life. 2. Trilingual Storyteller - The Thai Creator Who Speaks Thai, English & Chinese Fluently: Intersection: Multilingual content + Cultural storytelling + Humor + Social commentary. Why this niche works: You are trilingual, which is RARE among content creators. Most Thai influencers speak Thai/English, but very few add fluent Chinese into the mix. You naturally bridge three audiences (Thai, Chinese, and international viewers). You can use humor to explain cultural differences—making your content educational, fun, and globally relatable. Content Ideas: What Thai People Think About China vs. What Chinese People Think About Thailand, Speaking 3 Languages in One Video Challenge - Switching between Thai, English & Chinese while storytelling. Thai Phrases That Don't Make Sense in Chinese (and Vice Versal), How I Became Fluent in Chinese as a Thai Student - Personal language-learning journey. 3. Comedy Meets Culture - Using Humor to Make Cultural Differences Relatable: Intersection: Humor + Travel & Cultural Commentary + Relatable Lifestyle Content. Why this niche works: Many people love cultural commentary, but most content is serious or academic—you can make it FUNNY and relatable. Humor is universal and makes learning about different cultures more engaging. This would make you stand out from typical travel vlogs because your focus is funny cultural insights, not just sightseeing. Content Ideas: What Happens When a Thai Person Tries to Bargain in China - Funny interactions with vendors. Chinese People React to Thai Street Food - Bringing Chinese friends to Thai restaurants in China. Thai vs. Chinese Slang - Can You Guess the Meaning? - Explaining funny slang with humor. Culture Shock Moments That Made Me Think 'What is Life?'. Which Niche Should You Choose? Each of these has huge potential, but it depends on what feels most natural to you: If you love helping Thai students & professionals navigate life in China, go for Niche #1 (Thai in China). If you enjoy language and cultural storytelling, go for Niche #2 (Trilingual Storyteller). If you just love making people laugh while talking about cultural differences, go for Niche #3 (Comedy Meets Culture).
